items.text: States that an AI's percentage is an estimate of how often it expects to be right in similar cases, not a guarantee.
items.feedback_fail: Say what the number means: it is the AI's estimate of how often it would be right in similar cases — never a promise.

items.text: Explains that uncertainty remains because the system works from patterns in data, not from certainty.
items.feedback_fail: Add the 'why': the AI works from patterns in data, so some uncertainty always remains.

items.text: Gives an everyday example where a probabilistic answer is read correctly (e.g., weather, spam, map times).
items.feedback_fail: Ground it in one everyday example — weather chances, spam scores, or travel times work well.

items.text: Draws a practical consequence: a small stated risk still deserves a human look when the stakes matter.
items.feedback_fail: Close with the habit: when it matters, even a small stated risk deserves a person's attention.

anchors.pass_example: When the AI says 90%, it means it expects to be right about 90 times out of 100 in cases like this — not that it is sure this time. It works from patterns in data, so some doubt always remains. Like a 70% rain forecast: a dry day doesn't make it wrong. So when the stakes are real, even a small stated risk deserves a human look.
anchors.fail_example: Ninety percent means the AI checked 90% of the information and is basically certain, so you can treat the answer as fact.
